description: Mine radon (Rn-222) released by ventilation per tonne of coal mined, default for all countries without own factor
notes: Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): value is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. Centre = China typical 9.3e5 Bq/t (S0001 Table 26, para 101; =2.8 TBq/GWa at 3.0e6 t/GWa); high = China small mines 3.5e6; low = 1980s crude 36 GBq/GWa (S0008 para 178) / 3.0e6 t/GWa = 1.2e4 (the other crude figure, 600 GBq/GWa = 2.0e5, lies inside). Only China was measured; use for every other country and for 1800-1949 is extrapolation (mining depth, gas content and ventilation differ). Engine rule: a country-specific row (e.g. CHN) overrides the XWL row. Not exhalation from residues.

description: Mine radon (Rn-222) per tonne of coal mined, China measured
notes: Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): value is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. UNSCEAR 2016 Annex B Table 26: 23 mines in 8 provinces, ref. year about 2010; large 1.9e5, medium 1.3e6, small 3.5e6, typical 9.3e5 Bq/t. Window 2000-2025 only; earlier years fall back to the XWL row.

description: Radium-226 released in coal mine drainage per tonne of coal mined, Poland (Upper Silesian balance)
notes: Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): value is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. Release to rivers 400 (1987), 219 (1995), 120 (2003), 77 (2006) MBq/d (S0222; S0225 gives 225 for 1995) divided by Polish production of those years from data/activity coal_production_t POL (S0804, whole country incl. lignite, so per-tonne values are diluted by about 25-30% against Silesian hard coal; applied to POL they reproduce the measured Bq/a). Low/high = observed spread of the four anchor years (falling with treatment); centre by the geometric-mean rule. No pre-1985 data and no other country: no row (gap).

description: Radium-228 released in coal mine drainage per tonne of coal mined, Poland (Upper Silesian balance)
notes: Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): value is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. Ra-228 release 380 (1995), 258 (2003), 170 (2006) MBq/d (S0222) over POL production; as for the Ra-226 row. Spread of three anchors.

description: Fraction of mobilised Ra-226 retained underground in Polish coal mines (precipitated deposits and sludge)
notes: Convention (METHODS 3.2, 4.1a, D24): value is for the HEAD nuclide of the group; the engine applies the group multiplier. CONFLICT carried as bounds: S0222 abstract over 70% stays underground; S0225 about 40%. Low 0.4, high 0.7, centre 0.55 (arithmetic, span <3x). Engine: retained = released x r/(1-r) using the Ra-226 drainage factor coal:0003 (formula is the stream spec's to confirm). Observation: S0222 balance (inflow about 650 vs 400 MBq/d released in 1987 = 38% retained; 77 in 2006 = 88%) suggests the two figures may be different years of improving treatment rather than a true source conflict. Tier set to impounded (coal_mining has no reisolated tier); Ra-228 assumed to behave like Ra-226 (analogy).

description: Ash-borne activity per tonne of fly ash from coal burned for power, U238+

description: Share of power-station ash (fly and bottom) to impounded: landfill, ash pond, dyke raising and land reclamation
notes: Unit-1 share applied to the ash-borne Bq after stack release; applies to both coal_fly_ash and coal_bottom_ash. Central values of the three tiers sum to 1.000 (impounded is the remainder); low/high are independent source bounds and need not sum to 1. No utilisation data before 1991 outside UNSCEAR: low 5% of ash to dwellings (S0008, US 1970s-80s), high about 40% (S0001 Fig. VII, US graph), centre geometric mean. The ACAA series (S0214, read 2026-10) starts in 1991 at about 25% of all US CCPs used, so US practice before 1991 was probably below 25%; the high bound is kept at 0.40 only to cover non-US practice (no non-US evidence for this era). Reisolated: no numeric share before 2000 (availability: no_data), high set to the India 2020-21 mine-filling share 6.2% (S0209); centre 0. ACAA (S0214) unreachable. Global average hides large country differences (US, India, China, EU).
